Hi Elena â€”

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + the two asks we discussed so we can finalize a pricing sketch for your finance team:

1) Confirm expected monthly active sessions and average prompt length (tokens in/out). We used a working assumption of 600k sessions/month and ~420 tokens average per session in the spreadsheet attached. If you have a narrower band that will change the unit economics a bit.

2) Confirm target effective price target (you mentioned a target of ~$700–900 per 1M tokens effective after any warm/session hits). We modeled $850 as a midpoint but can swing either way depending on hit-rate.

A few notes on the warm-layer model we walked through (attached: econ_scenarios_v1.xlsx):
- "Session warm-layer" = a small in-memory prefix store keyed by session ID that captures recent dialogue prefixes. It’s intentionally conservative compared to a full persistent LRU cache.
- Hit-rate sensitivity we used: 5%, 20%, 40% across three usage profiles (cold-first-message heavy, balanced, highly repetitive workflows).
- Effective $/1M tokens in the sheet assumes baseline hosted model unit cost $1,100/1M (no warm layer), and we show incremental cost reductions as a function of hit-rate and model variant (standard vs. quantized accel).

Can you confirm the session count and whether the team considers ~25% warm hits a realistic middle case? If yes, we’ll produce a single-slide econ summary and a short SOW for dedicated pilot capacity.

Attachments: econ_scenarios_v1.xlsx (model), session_warmback_diagram.png (architecture stub)

Thanks —
Monica

Monica —

Appreciate the quick recap. Some clarifications from our side after a short internal sync:

- Sessions: our ops dashboard shows ~520k sessions/month for production now, but we expect to ramp to 800k over the next 3 months with the new onboarding flow. For the first contract period we should price on expected steady-state of ~650k/month.
- Tokens: average currently ~380 tokens per session; with the updated prompts we expect ~420 as you modeled (so that assumption is fine).
- Warm hits: the product team thinks 15–30% is realistic for the most common flows (search + summarize patterns). 25% sounds reasonable as a mid-case.
- Your $700–900/1M target: CFO prefers to stay under $800 effective if possible; they asked whether a 25% hit-rate is enough to meet that target given the baseline $1,100/1M model cost.

Happy to run a short call with finance if you want them looped in. Also attaching our internal performance note (see inline) — we can share the SSO access for sample telemetry if needed.

Best,

Elena / Monica —

Thanks Elena. I pulled three quick scenarios into the attached sheet and pasted the summary below so it’s easy to forward to finance: (baseline model unit cost used: $1,100 per 1M tokens)

Scenarios (effective $/1M tokens after warm-layer savings):
- Conservative (15% warm hit, no quantization): $935/1M
- Mid (25% warm hit, 50% quantized inference split): $780/1M
- Aggressive (40% warm hit, 80% quantized split + reserved capacity): $610/1M

Notes:
- Warm hits only reduce tokenized compute when the warm prefix covers a substantive portion of the prompt. For summarization flows we measured that the warm prefix tends to be ~12–18% of tokens; for search-then-summarize flows it can be ~20–30%.
- Quantization assumptions: we modeled an incremental ~28% unit-cost reduction when routing 50% of tokens to a quantized runtime compatible with your accuracy SLA. Higher splits increase savings non-linearly when combined with higher hit-rates.
- Reserved capacity / Dedicated pools can reduce per-token baseline below $1,100 depending on commitment; sheet shows $950 baseline as a reserved example.

Action items I suggest:
1) Finance-friendly one-pager: Monica to draft a one-slide econ summary keyed to CFO questions (we’ll include the Conservative/Mid/Aggressive rows).
2) Pilot SOW draft: scope a 2-month pilot with session warm-layer enabled + telemetry capture so we can measure actual hit-rate by flow.
3) Quick finance call: proposed Thu Aug 26, 10:00am PT — confirm?

I attached econ_scenarios_v1.xlsx with the model variants and a short notes tab.

—Ben
